interpretive.rule: 'Property' includes intangible confidential business information — supports identity-credentials-as-property theory
Materiality is an element of §1343; natural-tendency-to-influence standard; identity misrepresentations inherently material
Scheme must target property; regulatory-authority schemes not covered; does not threaten financial property fraud cases

wire_fraud_pleading_checklist: Identify the scheme: what was the fraudulent plan and who devised it?
Identify the property object: what money/property was the scheme designed to obtain/deprive?
Identify the material misrepresentation: what false statement/omission was made? Is it material (would a reasonable person care)?
Identify each wire communication: date, medium (phone/email/EFT/online), content/purpose, interstate nexus
Map specific intent: evidence that the actor knew the representations were false and intended to defraud
operational_notes_for_steward_cases.count_strategy: Each wire communication in furtherance of the scheme = one §1343 count. In a complex identity theft scheme with multiple electronic account openings, wire transfers, and electronic inquiries, the count exposure can be very high. This drives plea leverage and referral priority.
operational_notes_for_steward_cases.rico_stacking: Multiple §1343 counts across Treasury + crypto + ChexSystems + Hillberg constitute related predicate acts satisfying RICO's pattern + continuity requirements. See civil_rico_1961_1968 standard for treble damages pathway.
